source_refs.note: Exercise 1.2, Question 2 (book p. 14): pick the transcendental functions; answer key p. 297

blocks.prompt: 2. Which of the following functions are transcendental? \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\), \(g(x) = \cot x\), \(h(x) = e^{2x} + \sqrt{x^{2}+2x}\), \(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}+e^{-x}}{2}\), \(r(x) = (x-1)^{-\frac{3}{2}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi classification ka sawal hai, magar is dafa humein transcendental functions chunne hain.
Diya kya hai? Paanch functions \(f, g, h, k, r\).
Find kya karna hai? In mein se transcendental kaun se hain.
Kaunsa rule? Function transcendental hai agar woh algebraic nahin, yani us mein trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic ya hyperbolic hissa ho jo hataya na ja sake.
Plan: har function ko parkhenge. Yaad rakhiye: \(x\) ki negative ya fractional power bhi algebraic hi hai; asal pehchaan yeh hai ke variable power mein hai ya base mein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\), \(g(x) = \cot x\), \(h(x) = e^{2x} + \sqrt{x^{2}+2x}\), \(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}+e^{-x}}{2}\), \(r(x) = (x-1)^{-3/2}\).
Maloom karna: in mein se transcendental kaun se hain.
Tareeqa: section 1.3 ke mutabiq jo algebraic nahin woh transcendental hai. Algebraic function \(x\) aur \(y\) ki polynomial equation satisfy karta hai; baqi wale \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(e^{x}\), \(\ln\) waghera rakhte hain. Har function par yahi kasauti lagayenge.

\(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\)
\[y = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[xy - 1 = 0\]
Algebraic hai, is liye transcendental nahin.
Kyun: yeh sirf taqseem hai (1 ko \(x\) se divide kiya). Cross-multiply karne se polynomial equation \(xy - 1 = 0\) mil gayi.

\(g(x) = \cot x\)
\[\cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\]
Transcendental.
Kyun: yeh trigonometric function hai; \(\cos x\) aur \(\sin x\) algebraic operations se nahin bante. Inhein angle se triangle ya circle ke zariye nikala jata hai, kisi polynomial se nahin.

\(h(x) = e^{2x} + \sqrt{x^{2}+2x}\)
Transcendental.
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x^{2}+2x}\) wala hissa algebraic hai, lekin \(e^{2x}\) exponential hai. Ab socho: agar \(h\) algebraic hota, to \(e^{2x} = h(x) - \sqrt{x^{2}+2x}\) do algebraic functions ka farq hota, aur woh bhi algebraic hota, jo ghalat hai. Is liye algebraic hissa jorne se exponential hissa khatam nahin hota.
Dhyan dein: sirf aadha function dekh kar faisla mat kijiye; poore function mein ek bhi transcendental hissa ho to woh transcendental hai.

\(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}+e^{-x}}{2}\)
\[k(x) = \cosh x\]
Transcendental.
Kyun: yeh exponentials \(e^{x}\) aur \(e^{-x}\) se bana hai; asal mein yeh \(\cosh x\) hai.

\(r(x) = (x-1)^{-3/2}\)
\[y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x-1)^{3}}}\]
\[y^{2} = \dfrac{1}{(x-1)^{3}}\]
\[(x-1)^{3}y^{2} - 1 = 0\]
Algebraic hai, is liye transcendental nahin.
Kyun: is mein sirf power, root aur taqseem hai. Variable \(x\) base mein hai, power mein nahin. Square kar ke cross-multiply karne se polynomial equation mil gayi.
Dhyan dein: ajeeb si power \(-\frac{3}{2}\) dekh kar log ise transcendental keh dete hain; yeh ghalat hai.
Tasdeeq: answer key bhi \(g\), \(h\) aur \(k\) ko transcendental batati hai. Jawab mil gaya.
blocks.final_answer: Transcendental functions \(g(x) = \cot x\), \(h(x) = e^{2x} + \sqrt{x^{2}+2x}\) aur \(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}+e^{-x}}{2}\) hain. (\(f\) aur \(r\) algebraic hain.)
